case_name: G. Mohan v State By Cbi
respondent:
State By Cbi, Bangalore
Supreme Court of India

17 August 2004
Cr.A. No. 83 of 1999
The Order of the Court was as follows:
Heard the parties.
1. On appeal being preferred, the High Court confirmed the conviction. Hence, this appeal by special leave.
2. facts: The appellant was convicted by the trial court under Section 5(1)(d) read with Section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 and Section 165 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
On appeal being preferred, the High Court confirmed the conviction.
The present case is not a case of direct evidence, but it is a case of circumstantial evidence
The two courts below have come to the conclusion after threadbare discussion of evidence
issues: Whether the payment of price was made by the person in whose favour refund order was passed and the price was paid for no other purpose except by way of illegal gratification to the appellant in kind.
court_reasoning: It is well settled that even in cases under the Prevention of Corruption Act, it is not necessary that the prosecutor is required to prove its case only by direct evidence and the same can be based upon circumstantial evidence alone.
The two courts below have come to the conclusion after threadbare discussion of evidence
holding: The appeal, accordingly, fails and is dismissed as such.
Bail bonds of the appellant, who is on bail, are cancelled and he is directed to be taken into custody forthwith to serve remaining period of sentence.
